tasks.title: Version Developer MCP audit records for staged trusted context
tasks.objective: Repair the contract conflict exposed by DEV-MCP-TM009-07 run 1 before retrying the append. At immutable seed commit 83eee2fa6537d1659359b8555f5f38638977ab6d, the sixteen-field v1 schema requires non-null tool, slug, actor, resource and risk identity, so early denials cannot be represented without inventing identity. Before launching the restricted implementation agent, the trusted controller runs the first two verification entries in its independent sandbox. Together they must prove the seed exists; the seed field/type shape is v1; the exact direct TypeScript consumers under packages/developer-mcp/src; the exact code-root consumer of DeveloperMcpCallDenialCode at the seed and its bounded current consumer set; and the absence of dependencies, optionalDependencies, peerDependencies and bundledDependencies in both manifests. The agent must not rerun those premise commands and the controller must stop before launch if either fails. DeveloperMcpAuditRecord and assertDeveloperMcpAuditRecord remain directly referenced only by audit.ts and contracts.test.ts throughout this schema-only task; call-authorization derives only the shared decision-code type and call-authorization.test adds its compile-time equality proof. Replace schema v1 with the closed v2 tagged union recorded by the 2026-08-05 owner plan: contextResolution is unresolved, principal or complete; decisionCode is allowed or one of the exact call-denial codes; and each stage retains exactly the identity already validated at that decision point. This amendment adds neither append nor route behavior.
acceptanceCriteria: DEVELOPER_MCP_AUDIT_FIELDS is snapshotted as one exact closed list containing the original sixteen names plus contextResolution and decisionCode. schemaVersion accepts only the literal "2"; a v1 record is rejected so two meanings never share one version.

DeveloperMcpAuditDecisionCode is the single exported vocabulary for "allowed", "invalid_context", "unknown_tool", "authority_missing", "resource_denied" and "revoked". DeveloperMcpCallDenialCode derives from it rather than repeating a second hand-maintained union, and a compile-time exhaustive test fails when either side drifts.

DeveloperMcpAuditRecord is exported as a compile-time discriminated union over contextResolution and decisionCode, not as one object type with optional fields. Compile-time assertions cover every identity field at every stage: toolName, slug, profileVersion, clientId, userId, tenantId, resourceType, resourceId and riskClass. Unresolved makes all nine exactly null; principal makes toolName, slug, profileVersion and riskClass exactly null and the five actor/resource fields non-null; complete makes every field except profileVersion non-null, with profileVersion narrowed per decision.

The unresolved stage is legal only for invalid_context, authorizationDecision deny, outcome denied, revocationCheckResult not_required and profileVersion null. Its toolName, slug, clientId, userId, tenantId, resourceType, resourceId and riskClass are all null, so malformed input cannot leak untrusted raw values or acquire fabricated identity.

The principal stage is legal only for invalid_context after principal/resource validation but failed authority-timestamp validation, unknown_tool, or authority_missing before descriptor resolution. clientId, userId and tenantId must each be non-empty, at most 128 code units, already trimmed, and contain only printable ASCII bytes 0x20 through 0x7e, exactly matching call-authorization.ts boundedString. resourceType must be exactly module_project or module_workspace and resourceId exactly 32 lowercase hexadecimal characters, matching call-authorization.ts validResource. toolName, slug, profileVersion and riskClass are null; authorization is deny, revocation is not_required and outcome is denied. This retains attributable validated actor/resource identity without copying an unvalidated raw tool name.

The complete stage is legal only for allowed, authority_missing, resource_denied or revoked. clientId, userId and tenantId obey the exact call-authorization.ts boundedString grammar; resourceType and resourceId obey the exact call-authorization.ts validResource grammar, including 32 lowercase hexadecimal resourceId. toolName, slug and riskClass are non-null and agree with the frozen descriptor. resourceType records the validated requested resource. It may differ from the descriptor for authority_missing because effective-authority denial precedes the comparison, or for resource_denied when that comparison caused denial; allowed and revoked require an exact match.

Descriptor agreement is load-bearing for all twelve tools. A literal table in contracts.test.ts lists every toolName with its exact slug, riskClass and descriptor resourceType; an assertion against the frozen catalogue fails if a descriptor is added, removed or reordered without a literal row. For every row, an otherwise-valid complete record validates, then independently changing slug or riskClass to another valid enum rejects. Changing requested resourceType rejects for allowed and revoked, while authority_missing and resource_denied follow their explicitly permitted mismatch rules.

tasks.objective: Add a bounded tenant-authorized brand document upload transaction that preserves byte provenance and creates a reviewable proposal without auto-approval or apply.
acceptanceCriteria: A distinct same-origin upload action enforces brand.proposal.upload, requires separate same-tenant brand.proposal.supersede authority before replacing a live draft, bounds bytes before materializing the file, and applies the parser's 256 KiB, 64-key, media, and encoding rules.
The transaction computes provenance from original bytes, uses the registered parser version, stores recognized values for review, and never fetches embedded URLs, renders HTML, or invokes a model.
Duplicate, re-upload, superseded, tenant-scope, immutable-digest, parser-failure, lock, and transactional audit semantics match the accepted PRD.
Tests use disposable PostgreSQL fixtures for success, invalid files, races, audit rollback, and lock handling; upload never auto-approves or auto-applies.
The page read model returns bounded typed source kind, original digest, parser version, and attribution for uploads and legacy URL proposals without raw document content.

tasks.title: Unify Assessment save, restore, and export
tasks.objective: Use one versioned tenant-scoped Assessment document for live persistence, explicit restore, report export, respondents, and stale-aware readouts while preserving legacy data.
acceptanceCriteria: The versioned mapping validates client fields, scores, evidence, respondents, progress, and readout and clearly separates report JSON from a restorable engagement document.
Readout state persists with its input binding, restores without a model call, becomes visibly stale after relevant edits, and is replaced only by explicit successful regeneration.
The repository becomes the live provider persistence boundary; legacy blobs remain until validated conversion is saved and corrupt or ambiguous data keeps a recovery path.
New storage uses server-supplied tenant context, while passcode mode retains documented browser-local ownership and does not invent a durable user identity.
Import validates before replacing state, and tests cover conversion, reload, round trip, evidence, full storage, demo isolation, same-origin tenant switching, invalid input, and failed generation.
Browser evidence proves actual downloads and restored state. Rollback preserves readable legacy backups and new documents.
